tasks.short: Review event notes and isolate the pertinent facts.

steps.what: Read notes taken about the news event
Read mail that adds facts about the event
Read the assignment brief beside the notes
Pull candidate facts from the event notes

loop.output: candidate facts, each with the note span it came from
loop.check: drop any candidate whose words are not in the notes
loop.stop: stop when every remaining candidate has a span, or when none remain; if the notes are not text, return nothing
loop.why_not_simpler: the notes are prose, so a field compare cannot find the facts

steps.what: Decide which notes hold the pertinent facts
Record the accepted facts on the story notes
Talk through the pertinent details with the editor

tasks.design: The reporter reads the event notes in {DOCS}, related mail in {EMAIL}, and the assignment brief in {CMS}. A bounded pass lists factual lines and keeps a line only when the same words are in the notes. The reporter decides which lines are pertinent, records that list on the story notes, and still talks the details through with the editor.
tasks.previous_blocker: The notes are prose, so a field compare could not list the factual lines.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded pass can keep a line only when the same words are in the notes, and the reporter still decides which lines are pertinent.
tasks.still_hard: Shorthand, a fact that is implied rather than written, and whether the detail is pertinent.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter can tell a pertinent fact from colour that happens to be written in the notes.
tasks.altitude: Marking every factual line in the notes leaves this part of the week. Reading the notes, deciding pertinence, recording the list and the talk with the editor stay.

reach.task: Mark the pertinent facts in an interview
reach.learn: Which detail is colour and which detail is the fact.

evidence.claim: A bounded pass can list sentences in a reporter's notes and drop any sentence that is not already written there.
A former editor was suspended because quotes in blog posts had been invented by a tool.
A 2026 journalists' guideline says not to put confidential or personal data into such tools, and to report the use to the editorial council.

assumptions: Prompt means sum to 100: screens 3.1, spreadsheets 3.6, mail 5.3, documents 72.9, meetings 15.1. Largest remainder gives screens 3, spreadsheets 4, mail 5, documents 73, meetings 15.
This task's notes are documents, so the spreadsheet 4 moves onto documents. Documents 77 are s1 40, s4 20, s5 12 and s6 5. Screens 3 are s3. Mail 5 is s2. Meetings 15 are s7.
Boundary: s1 starts on the notes; s2 and s3 change means; s4 produces the candidate list; s5 is the pertinence decision; s6 records that decision; s7 is a live talk with the editor.
The pass reads only notes already stored as text in {DOCS}. Handwritten notes are out of the pass and stay in s1.
No house list of pertinent facts is maintained. The sentences are already in that event's notes. Keeping such a list would be the reporter's work, and this design does not add it.
The editor talk is inside the desk. It does not send the fact list outside, and it does not hold the gate. The gate sits on the record of the accepted list.
Publishing the story is a different task and is not counted here.
The suspension case is why a candidate with no note span is dropped. That case is not a share of this task, and it is not used in the range.

Low is handwritten notes or notes not cleared for the tool, so the pass returns nothing. High keeps the pass and drops about eight points for shorthand the span check cannot read. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of notes.
unknowns: Whether this desk's event notes are typed in the document store or stay on paper.
Which notes the desk has already cleared under the journalists' guideline.
Whether the editorial council must be told before the pass is used on notes.
research_questions: Are event notes stored as text the pass can read?
What share of notes is shorthand or still on paper?
Who clears notes before they may be read by the pass?

already_counted.description: The pertinence decision is the whole of the check step and is not extra upkeep.

incremental.description: No house list of pertinent facts is maintained. Each run reads that event's notes and drops a line with no note span.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is handwritten notes or notes not cleared for the tool, so the pass returns nothing and the saving is zero. High keeps the pass and drops about eight points because shorthand has no clean span. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive assignments and evaluate leads into story ideas.

steps.what: Receive the desk assignment for a new story
Read leads and tips for a possible story
Read background notes before choosing a story
Read the story subjects already on the desk
Evaluate which leads to develop as a story
Write the accepted story ideas onto the assignment

tasks.design: The reporter receives the assignment in the desk meeting, reads leads in {EMAIL}, background in {DOCS}, and the subjects already on the desk in {CMS}. The reporter decides which lead becomes the story idea. That accepted idea is written on the assignment. No pass chooses the story.
tasks.previous_blocker: A subject line does not say whether a tip is a story.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in the existing desk tools removes that judgement, so the meeting and the write stay with the reporter.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the lead is worth the desk's day, and what the editor will accept.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter can tell a tip that is a story from one that only repeats a subject already on the desk.
tasks.altitude: The story choice stays in the meeting. Nothing in this task leaves the week, and the reporter does not gain a right to assign the desk.

reach.task: Choose which tip becomes an item
reach.learn: How a lead is tested before it is treated as a story.

evidence.claim: Choosing a story from a lead is a judgement a stored subject line does not make, because the same subject can be a story one day and a repeat the next.

assumptions: Prompt means sum to 100: screens 4.8, spreadsheets 2.9, mail 15.0, documents 28.9, meetings 48.4. Largest remainder gives screens 5, spreadsheets 3, mail 15, documents 29, meetings 48.
Assignments and leads are not kept on a spreadsheet, so the spreadsheet 3 moves onto documents. Documents 32 are s3 16 and s6 16. Screens 5 are s4. Mail 15 is s2. Meetings 48 are s1 30 and s5 18.
Boundary: s1 starts at the desk meeting; s2, s3 and s4 change means; s5 is the story decision; s6 writes that decision onto the assignment.
s4 reads the subjects of stories already on the desk. It is not a search that replaces the decision.
No lead template is maintained. A stored subject does not decide the story, and keeping a scoring sheet would be the reporter's work. This design does not add one.
A reply to the person who sent a tip is a different task and is not counted here. The meeting is inside the desk and does not hold the gate. The gate sits on the write of the accepted idea.
Every step stays with the reporter, so the range is zero.
unknowns: Who on this desk is allowed to assign a story.
Whether a tip from outside must be answered inside this task.
Where the accepted story idea is written today.
research_questions: Does the desk meeting already produce a named assignment before the reporter writes the idea?
Are leads mostly mail, or mostly a phone call?
Is the accepted idea written on the assignment, or only remembered?

already_counted.description: Choosing the story idea is the whole of the check step and is not extra upkeep.

incremental.description: No lead template is maintained. The idea is decided in the meeting and written once.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The story decision, the reads and the write all stay with the reporter, so the saving is zero on both ends.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check reference materials to obtain the relevant facts.

steps.what: Read which relevant facts the notes still lack
Check the reference date and title stored
Find the passage in the stored news files
Read the passage to obtain the relevant facts
Decide which reference facts the passage supports
Record the accepted reference facts on the notes
Read mail that names the public records
Ask where the reference materials and books sit

tasks.design: The reporter reads which facts the notes still lack. The archive in {CMS} returns the stored news-file passage that contains the name and the date the reporter typed. The reporter reads that passage, or the book when the archive has no passage, decides the fact, and records it on the notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fact sat somewhere in a long news file, and the reporter had to hunt for the passage.
tasks.enabler_now: The archive can return the passage that contains the name and the date, and the reporter still reads that passage.
tasks.still_hard: A fact that is only in a book, a public record that is not in the archive, and whether the passage is the right fact.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter can tell that a passage states the fact the story needs, rather than a similar name or an older date.
tasks.altitude: Hunting a news file that is already in the archive leaves this part of the week. Reading the passage, deciding the fact, and checking books stay.

reach.role: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
reach.task: Check a name and a date before a bulletin
reach.learn: How to read the passage rather than a retelling of it.

evidence.claim: A news archive that already stores the article can return the passage containing a name and a date the reporter typed, without writing a new sentence.
In a study with a public broadcaster, 45 percent of assistant answers about news had a significant issue.

assumptions: Prompt means sum to 100.1: screens 2.4, spreadsheets 3.3, mail 5.0, documents 67.7, meetings 21.7. Scaled by 100/100.1 and then largest remainder, they are screens 2, spreadsheets 3, mail 5, documents 68, meetings 22.

Reference materials are books, news files and records, not a spreadsheet, so the spreadsheet 3 moves onto documents. Documents 71 are s1 16, s3 24, s4 16, s5 10 and s6 5. Screens 2 are s2. Mail 5 is s7. Meetings 22 are s8.
Boundary: s1 starts from the missing fact; s2, s4, s7 and s8 change means; s3 returns the passage; s5 decides the fact; s6 records it.

s3 uses the archive search the desk already has. It returns the stored passage and does not write a sentence. s2 reads the stored date and title of that file, which is content, not an open-by-identifier stop.
The structured input is the name and the date the reporter typed in s1. If the archive has no passage, s3 returns nothing and s4 reads the book.
No reference map is maintained. Typing the name and the date for this check is already inside s1. A person keeping a map of sources would be human work, and this design does not add that job.

An assistant that answers from the archive is rejected because assistants misrepresent news. The 45 percent figure is that study's finding. It is not a share of this task and is not used in the range.
Checking a fact for the story notes is this task. Publishing the story is not.
The colleague question about where a book sits is inside the desk. It does not hold the gate. The gate sits on the record of the accepted fact.

Low is a fact that is only in a printed book or a public record outside the archive, so the hunt stays manual. High keeps the archive hunt and drops about ten points for files with no name and date to match. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of checks.
unknowns: Whether this desk's news files are already in the archive.
Which public records the archive does not hold.
research_questions: Does the archive search return a passage, or only a headline?
What share of these checks is a printed book rather than a stored news file?
Are the name and the date already typed before the hunt starts?

already_counted.description: Judging that the passage supports the fact is the whole of the check step and is not extra upkeep.

incremental.description: No reference map is maintained. The reporter types the name and the date for this check, and that time is already in the read.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a fact only in a printed book or a public record outside the archive, so the saving is zero. High keeps the archive hunt and drops about ten points because many files have no name and date to match. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine the story emphasis, length and format.

steps.what: Read the material gathered for this story
Determine emphasis, length and format for the story
Arrange gathered material under the story emphasis

loop.input: story material and the accepted story shape
loop.output: an order of points taken from the material
loop.check: drop any line that is not one of the supplied points
loop.stop: stop when every line matches a supplied point, or when the order is empty; if the material is not text, return nothing
loop.why_not_simpler: the material is prose, so a fixed sort cannot tell which point serves the emphasis

steps.what: Check the ordered material against the emphasis
Record the broadcasted emphasis, length and format
Read mail about the published story length
Read the section length stored for this desk

tasks.design: The reporter reads the material in {DOCS}, the length note in {EMAIL}, and the section length in {CMS}, then decides emphasis, length and format in the meeting. A bounded pass orders only points already in the material under that emphasis and drops any new line. The reporter checks the order and records the plan. The story is not published in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ordering prose by hand was the only way to line the material up with an emphasis.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the reporter has chosen the emphasis, a bounded pass can order only the points already in the material.
tasks.still_hard: The emphasis itself, the length a broadcast can carry, and whether a point really serves that emphasis.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter can choose the emphasis and can tell that an ordered point does not actually serve it.
tasks.altitude: Reordering points already chosen leaves this part of the week. The emphasis, the length, the format and the check of the order stay with the reporter.

reach.task: Set a bulletin item's length and emphasis
reach.learn: How the running order follows the emphasis the editor chose.

evidence.claim: Once a person has chosen an emphasis, a bounded pass can order points that are already written in the material and drop a line that is not one of those points.
A former editor was suspended because quotes in blog posts had been invented by a tool.

assumptions: Prompt means sum to 100.1: screens 2.3, spreadsheets 1.5, mail 6.8, documents 61.4, meetings 28.1. Scaled by 100/100.1 and then largest remainder, they are screens 2, spreadsheets 2, mail 7, documents 61, meetings 28.
The story material is a document, so the spreadsheet 2 moves onto documents. Documents 63 are s1 22, s3 18, s4 14 and s5 9. Meetings 28 are s2. Mail 7 is s6. Screens 2 are s7.
Boundary: s1 starts on the material; s6 and s7 change means; s2 is the emphasis decision; s3 produces the order; s4 checks that order; s5 records the plan.
The pass may use only the points in the story material and the emphasis, length and format from s2. It may not add a line. s4 checks that the order serves the emphasis.

No format template is maintained. The emphasis, length and format are chosen for this story in the meeting. A person who keeps a standing format list is doing human work, and this task does not add that upkeep. s7 only reads a section length that is already stored.
The meeting decides the shape and does not hold the gate. The gate sits on the record of the accepted plan. Publishing the story is a different task.
The suspension case is why a new line is dropped. That case is not a share of this task and is not used in the range.

Low is material that is not yet a set of points the reporter has separated, so the pass returns nothing. High keeps the ordering and drops about eight points when the piece is a broadcast script the point order does not fit. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of stories.
unknowns: Whether a second person must accept the plan before it is recorded.
Whether broadcast length differs by programme on this desk.
Whether the section length in {CMS} is kept by this reporter or by another role.
research_questions: Is the material already split into points before the emphasis is chosen?
Does this desk record the plan before anyone writes the story?
Who keeps the section length, if anyone?

already_counted.description: Checking the order against the emphasis is the whole of the check step and is not extra upkeep.

incremental.description: No format template is maintained. Emphasis, length and format are chosen for this story in the meeting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is material that is not yet separated into points, so the pass returns nothing and the saving is zero. High keeps the ordering and drops about eight points when a broadcast script does not fit a point order. Both figures are assumptions, not a count of stories.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week keeps the pertinence call, the story choice, and the reading of the passage. Marking every factual line in the notes, hunting a news file already in the archive, and reordering points already chosen leave the week. The reporter does not gain a right to publish an unchecked fact.
reach: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
skills_to_grow: Tell a pertinent fact from a colour detail.
Judge whether a lead is a story.
Match an emphasis to the material in hand.
role.ambitious_version: The reporter spends the desk meeting on which story to run, not on hunting a passage already in the archive.
